title: B. F. Skinner's birth chart
metaDescription: B. F. Skinner's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 29.7° Pisces. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 8.8° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 29.7° Pisces, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Mars. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 23.7° Pisces, Venus holds 1.3° Pisces, Mars holds 17.2° Aries — in the old shorthand, thought steeped in tone and memory; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars sextile Saturn, 0.1° of separation. A sextile pays out only on effort; the scheme calls it opportunity rather than gift. Behind it, the Sun square Uranus at 0.2°, and Venus sextile Uranus at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Uranus opposes Neptune while both square the Sun. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, five placements stand out. The Moon in Taurus at 8.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mercury in Pisces at 23.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Venus in Pisces at 1.3° is in exaltation; Mars in Aries at 17.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Saturn in Aquarius at 17.1° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 3, fire 3, air 2, earth 1, and mutable 4, cardinal 3, fixed 2 across the modes. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. the Sun crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day, so its sign is left open. The day carried no retrograde motion at all; everything moved forward as seen from here.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.6° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 8.8°.
